thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 — 12m spike, 18% error-rate, customer-visible latency increases. alert id: ALERT-5XX-EUW-314 (auto-created)

Jess (SRE): Acked. I'm on it. Can someone drop the quick impact: count of affected customers and top routes?

Miguel (oncall): Oncall here too. Seeing lots of gateway timeouts coming from model-proxy-2 (502s) and some 504s from the upstream provider. Dashboard shows 504 latency tail increasing ~10s for some requests.

Sam (runtime): Pushed a small change to proxy routing yesterday — rolling back to previous route now. Command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-proxy -n inference`

Jess (SRE): Good call. Rolling back now. I'll also scale the pool for eu-west-1 by +2 replicas while rollback completes: `./infra scale --pool inference-eu --delta 2`

observability-bot: Rollout undo started (model-proxy v4 -> v3). Scale request accepted; target replicas increased from 6 -> 8.

Miguel (oncall): Noted. I'm going to enable the fallback route (route policy: degrade -> small-model-quant) for all requests > 8s latency so customer calls at least return. Patch: `PATCH /routes/degrade -> set fallback: small-quant`

Sam (runtime): Degrade routing applied. Confirmed traffic split: primary 92% / fallback 8%.

Jess (SRE): After rollback and fallback applied, error-rate dropped to 6% in the next 3 minutes. Still above SLO but much better. We should evaluate alert thresholds — current alert is `error_rate > 5% for 5m` which is noisy during partial upstream outages.

Olivia (product): FYI, support ticket queue shows some customers reported failed uploads in last 30m. Severity 2 for a handful of affected accounts. We should include communication note if this becomes prolonged.

Miguel (oncall): Agree. From on-call perspective, the alert firing threshold needs refinement: we get noisy pages for short-lived spikes that auto-heal with fallback. Suggest change to `error_rate > 8% for 10m` and a separate `gateway-timeout-aggregation` alert: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",route!="/health"}[1m])) by (region) > X` with annotation about upstream provider.

Jess (SRE): Quick triage summary: root cause appears to be transient packet drops between model-proxy-2 and upstream model-serving in eu-west-1 causing request retry storms and queue pileups. Rollback removed the new routing behavior that exposed the upstream flap.

Sam (runtime): Logs show increased `retry_count` and `connection_reset` on proxy instance model-proxy-2 around 2432109300. Extract: ```
[2432109301] WARN retry attempt=3 route=model-proxy-2 upstream=upstream-edge-7 error=connection_reset
[2432109302] ERROR handler request_id=... status=502
```

observability-bot: Alert suppressed: ALERT-5XX-EUW-314 -> auto-suppressed after mitigation.

Jess (SRE): Action items for post-incident:
- create ticket to tune alerting: raise 5xx threshold to 8% and increase evaluation window to 10m, add region-scoped aggregation (eu-west-1).
- add a new dashboard panel showing `upstream latency` + `proxy retry_count` side-by-side and an annotation layer for rollouts.
- add runbook step to enable fallback-route automatically when `avg_latency > 6s` AND `error_rate > 5%` for 3m so mitigation happens before paging.

Miguel (oncall): I'll own the alert tuning ticket and the runbook PR. Creating NOW: https://tickets/internal/RED-3456 (placeholder)

Olivia (product): Please include a short blurb for support: what to tell customers if they ask. Suggested: "We observed intermittent timeouts in eu-west-1 that caused request failures for a subset of traffic. We routed affected requests to a smaller fallback model while we stabilized the upstream provider. Most requests succeeded after fallback was applied."

Sam (runtime): For the alert expression proposal, copying here for visibility:```
# Firing when 5xx exceed 8% over 10m OR gateway timeout spikes
firing_5xx = (sum(rate(http_requests_total{region="eu-west-1",status=~"5.."}[10m]))
 / sum(rate(http_requests_total{region="eu-west-1"}[10m]))) > 0.08

gateway_timeout = increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{status="504",region="eu-west-1"}[5m]) > 20
```
Combine with `FOR: 10m` and set severity=page only if `firing_5xx AND gateway_timeout` OR `firing_5xx > 0.15` to avoid pages for small blips.

Jess (SRE): That looks reasonable. Also add an annotation to the alert: `recommended_action: enable_fallback` and a link to the rollback playbook.

Miguel (oncall): Working on PR for the alert rule and dashboard. I'll link PRs here. Also will adjust mute rules so that notification escalation goes to a dedicated slack channel `#incident-paging` for multi-region incidents.

observability-bot: New dashboard draft created: `EUW - Proxy Health & Upstream Latency (draft)`. Link: https://dashboards.internal/d/xyz

Jess (SRE): Before closing: confirm customer impact numbers. Olivia, can you post the list of affected customers and severity?

Olivia (product): Posted in the support thread: 7 accounts saw errors, 2 accounts saw degraded latency but successful calls. No revenue-critical SLA customers reported outages yet. Support note locked and sent to priority queue.

Miguel (oncall): Follow-up plan (next 24h): 1) merge alert tuning PR, 2) add dashboard panel and link into the alert, 3) schedule postmortem if we see recurrence > 1/week, 4) reach out to upstream provider to investigate packet drops.

Jess (SRE): Marking this incident as mitigated. I'll update the incident-bot with close status in 15m if no regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident ALERT-5XX-EUW-314 marked mitigated by Jess (SRE). Please file postmortem if there was customer impact.

Miguel (oncall): Filing post-incident ticket with context and attaching logs. Ticket: https://tickets/internal/RED-3457

Sam (runtime): Adding a note to the deployment checklist: don't roll routing changes during peak hours in a region without extra canary capacity.

Olivia (product): Thanks team. Let me know if support needs a postmortem-ready summary for customers.

Jess (SRE): Closing thread in 30m if stable.

(reacted :thumbsup: by Miguel (oncall), :eyes: by Olivia (product))
